name: Lying Cable Chest Press
description: A chest press performed lying on the floor or a flat bench with cable machines positioned at floor level on each side. Unlike dumbbell or barbell pressing, the cable provides constant resistance throughout the full range of motion, including at full extension where free weights would have zero loading. The lying position limits the range (the floor prevents the elbows from dropping below body level) but the cable tension at lockout provides a unique stimulus at the top of the press that free weights cannot replicate.

execution.starting_position: Lie on the floor or a flat bench positioned between two low cable pulleys. Hold the D-handles of the cables with hands at chest level, elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees.
execution.setup_instructions: Position the bench between two cable stacks with the cables at their lowest setting. Adjust so the cables come from low and to the sides, pulling the handles outward and downward at the bottom of the press.
steps: Step 1: Lie with handles at chest level, elbows bent and in contact with the floor (floor press) or just above chest level (bench).
Step 2: Press both handles upward and together, extending the elbows and squeezing the pecs at the top.
Step 3: Hold at full extension with the handles together — the cable tension remains at lockout.
Step 4: Lower under control back to the start. Repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale as you lower. Exhale during the press.
common_mistakes: Cables positioned too high, reducing the loading at the bottom
Losing scapular retraction at lockout — maintain shoulder blade position throughout
Pressing one side faster than the other, creating rotation
safety_considerations: Ensure both cable stacks are at the same weight
If using the floor, the elbows cannot go below body level — this limits ROM but reduces shoulder stress
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full elbow extension at the top. For floor press: elbows to floor level at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Feel the cable pulling inward at the top — squeeze the chest hard to control it
Keep the shoulder blades retracted on the bench throughout the press
Equal weight on both sides — do not let one arm lead
